vc_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the subscription documents for our fund's closing. This is drafting/preparation work only — a human must explicitly approve before anything is sent to LPs or applied.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already provided, including: the fund's legal name and entity type, jurisdiction of formation, GP/manager name, target fund size and minimum commitment amount, the fund's counsel firm (if any prior subscription document template exists), the current LP list with names, entities, and proposed commitment amounts, key terms (management fee, carry, hurdle if any), and the closing date(s) planned (first close / final close).

Using that information, draft the subscription document package: the subscription agreement, investor questionnaire (covering accreditation/qualified purchaser status, AML/KYC representations, tax certifications such as W-9/W-8 as applicable), and a signature page template that maps to the final LP schedule. Where legal language requires specialized drafting (e.g., specific representations, side letter references, jurisdiction-specific clauses), flag those sections clearly as needing attorney review rather than inventing legal text.

Organize the output as a clean draft package (e.g., a shared document or exported files) with a summary memo listing: each LP, proposed commitment amount, and any open questions or missing data per LP.

Do not send anything to LPs, do not finalize or execute any document, and do not mark any commitment as accepted. When the draft package and summary memo are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off before any subscription documents are distributed or applied.

vc_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me send subscription documents to our fund's LPs for signature using {{vendor}}, our legal-ops e-signature platform. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the final LP list with names, emails, and commitment amounts, (2) the subscription document template (or confirm the version to use), (3) my {{vendor}} account access (use my configured credentials), and (4) any specific signing order, deadline, or reminder cadence I want applied.

Once you have these, do the following in {{vendor}}: prepare the subscription packet by merging each LP's name, commitment amount, and any LP-specific fields into the template; set up a bulk send so each LP receives their own correctly populated packet rather than a single shared document; configure signing order if any LP must sign before others, set an expiration date for outstanding signature requests, and enable automatic reminders for non-responders. If {{vendor}} exposes an API or similar programmatic interface for generating, populating, and dispatching these documents, use it to reduce manual entry, otherwise use the dashboard equivalent.

Prepare a complete draft send — populated documents for every LP, the recipient list, signing order, reminder/expiration settings — and present it to me as a summary for review, including a sample of one populated document so I can confirm accuracy before anything goes out.

Do not actually dispatch, submit, or trigger the send to any LP. This requires my explicit approval, so stop for human sign-off once the draft package and settings are ready for my review. Report back with: the number of LPs queued, the settings configured, any LPs missing required data, and a clear confirmation that no documents have been sent yet.

vc_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me track the LP signature-collection step of closing our fund. Each LP needs to review and execute their own subscription documents on their own timeline — the actual signing remains a human step and cannot be accelerated by you.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) the list of LPs and their contact emails, (2) which e-signature or document-distribution service we're using (e.g., DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or email with PDF), (3) the current status of each LP's subscription document (sent / viewed / signed / outstanding) if I have it, and (4) the target close date I'm working toward.

Once I provide this, please:
1. Build or update a simple tracking sheet (or use one I point you to) listing each LP, document sent date, current signature status, and any outstanding items.
2. Draft polite, professional follow-up/reminder emails for any LPs whose documents are outstanding past a reasonable window (e.g., 5–7 business days), referencing the target close date.
3. If our e-signature service has a dashboard or status-check capability, check it using your configured credentials to pull current completion status for each LP and update the tracking sheet accordingly.
4. Flag any LPs who appear stalled or non-responsive so I can decide on manual outreach.

Do not send any reminder emails or communications on my behalf — prepare the drafts and the updated tracker, then stop for human sign-off before anything goes out.

Report back with: the updated LP status tracker, the drafted reminder emails (labeled by recipient), and a summary noting how many LPs have signed, how many are outstanding, and any LPs flagged as at-risk for the close timeline. Note explicitly that final signature timing rests with the LPs and remains a human step outside our control.

vc_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the Amended & Restated Limited Partnership Agreement (A&R LPA) for our fund's closing, incorporating the final LP schedule of committed investors. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the original/current LPA document (file or link), (b) the final list of LPs with committed capital amounts, admission dates, and any side-letter terms, (c) any negotiated changes since the last draft (fee terms, key-person provisions, advisory committee composition, etc.), and (d) the word processor or document platform I use (e.g., Microsoft Word, Google Docs) so you can work in that format.
2. Using the base LPA and the inputs I give you, draft the Amended & Restated LPA: update the LP schedule/exhibit with each LP's name, commitment amount, and admission date; incorporate any negotiated legal or economic changes as tracked edits or a clearly marked redline; and flag any inconsistencies between side letters and the main agreement text.
3. Produce a clean version and a redline/comparison version showing all changes from the prior LPA.
4. Prepare a short summary memo listing: total commitments, number of LPs, and every substantive change made from the original agreement, so I can review quickly.
5. Do NOT finalize, execute, distribute for signature, or apply any changes as binding — this step requires a human to explicitly approve the draft before it is applied. After preparing the redline, clean draft, and summary memo, stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the location/filenames of the clean draft and redline, the summary memo of changes, and a list of any open questions or discrepancies (e.g., mismatched commitment figures, missing side-letter references) that need my decision before approval.

vc_002:n4b.prompt:
You are helping me track and prepare for the execution of the fund's Amended & Restated Limited Partnership Agreement (A&R LPA) by the GP and all LPs. This closing document finalizes the fund terms and the final LP schedule, and signature collection depends on each external counterparty returning countersigned pages — the actual act of the GP and every LP signing remains a human step that no single portal or agent action can complete.

Please do the following preparatory and monitoring work:

1. Ask me for: the final A&R LPA document (or its location), the complete LP schedule with names, commitment amounts, and contact/signatory emails, and whichever e-signature or document-distribution service I'm using (e.g., DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or email with wet-ink/PDF signature) along with confirmation I have configured credentials for it.
2. Draft the distribution email/cover note to send the A&R LPA to the GP and each LP for signature, personalized with each party's name and commitment details from the schedule.
3. Prepare a signature-tracking checklist listing every required signatory (GP plus each LP), with columns for "sent," "signed," and "date received," so I can monitor status as pages come back.
4. If my configured e-signature service exposes a status-check or reporting feature, describe how to check outstanding/completed signatures via its dashboard or API, and offer to poll and summarize status for me on request (without submitting or finalizing anything).
5. Flag any missing LP contact information or document gaps that would block sending.

Do not sign, countersign, or mark any signature as complete on my behalf — this remains a human step for the GP and each LP to execute individually. Stop for human sign-off once the distribution drafts and tracking checklist are ready.

Report back with: the finalized distribution draft, the signatory tracking checklist, any gaps you found, and a summary of what remains outstanding for actual signature collection.

vc_002:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for the fund's first and final close (step vc_002:n5). This is a GP certification event requiring my explicit sign-off, so you must prepare all supporting materials but stop for human sign-off before any close is certified or filed.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the fund's legal name and entity details, (2) the final LP schedule with committed capital amounts per LP, (3) the location/repository where executed subscription documents and signature pages are stored, (4) the location of the executed amended & restated LPA, (5) bank account/wire confirmation details showing capital has been received, and (6) the target close date.

Using these inputs, please:
1. Compile a closing checklist confirming: all subscription documents are signed and countersigned, all LP signatures on the amended & restated LPA are collected, the final LP schedule matches signed subscriptions, and capital contributions have been confirmed as received (based on documentation I provide — do not attempt to verify bank transfers yourself).
2. Draft a closing certificate/GP certification memo stating that all conditions to closing have been satisfied, referencing the final LP schedule and total committed capital, formatted for GP review and signature.
3. Draft a closing notice to LPs confirming the close date and their final commitment amounts, ready for review.
4. Flag any discrepancies you find between the LP schedule, signed subscription documents, and stated capital contributions.

Once the checklist, certification memo, and LP notice drafts are ready, present them to me for review and stop for human sign-off — do not certify, sign, submit, or file anything on my behalf. Report back with the completed checklist, the drafted documents, and a list of any open items or discrepancies requiring my attention before I formally hold the close.
